Some of Patriot Platform's disruptive, eye-catching tactics seem to have been borrowed from environmental groups like Just Stop Oil. But its leaders are also getting ideas and funding from the growing "Christian nationalism" seen in the United States.

Its organisers say they are building a working-class "voting bloc" to persuade political parties on the right to adopt their agenda.

News.title: When an avalanche killed climber Nirmal Purja, his friends faced the hardest mission of all
News.content:
As he picked his way past the frozen slope towards two bodies, Mingma Gyalje Sherpa knew his friends were gone.

Together, the three of them had climbed the world's highest peaks, under crisp mountain skies and in treacherous snowstorms. Nirmal Purja and Kili Pemba Sherpa were two of the strongest climbers Mingma G had ever known.

But this July, an avalanche swept through Pakistan's Broad Peak while the two were on their way up, engulfing everything in its path.

The drone images seemed clear: no-one had survived.

And yet, as Mingma G came closer to the fluorescent down suits, sharp against the snow, he couldn't shake the idea they were waiting for him.

"I told them: 'It's ok. You don't have to be here in the cold anymore.'"

Speaking to the BBC in Islamabad, he recalls the terrible moment he reached for their bodies.

Holding one of them, he promised: "I'm here to take you guys home."

News.title: 'Skimpflation' warning as tinned mackerel alternative hits more supermarket shelves
News.content:
A growing trend of supermarkets selling a cheaper, less nutritious alternative to tinned mackerel is an example of "skimpflation", a consumer group has said.

Princes - which supplies major supermarkets - has substituted the fish for jack mackerel, an entirely different species also being sold by Lidl.

The switch has been spurred by dwindling stocks of Atlantic mackerel after years of overfishing, with its Chilean counterpart more sustainable and a third of the cost.

"It's a real concern when manufacturers quietly downgrade everyday staples like these as shoppers can end up paying the same price for a product that delivers significantly less nutritional quality," Sue Davies, head of food policy at Which?, said.

Jack mackerel contains about half as much omega-3 and around a third as much vitamin B12 as traditional mackerel.

The shift has prompted complaints from some consumers over differences in taste and texture, as well as concerns about how clearly the replacement fish is being labelled.

Princes announced last October, external that it was changing all of its tinned mackerel products to jack mackerel, saying the species meets the Marine Stewardship Council's sustainability standards.

The firm said its jack mackerel products were "clearly identified" and had been introduced following extensive product and consumer testing, describing it as having a "milder flavour and meatier texture".

Lidl is selling jack mackerel under its house brand. Lidl GB said it was "committed to sourcing fish and seafood from responsibly managed fisheries".

Davies from Which? said: "While manufacturers face genuine supply chain pressures and sustainability challenges, they have a responsibility to shoppers to be completely upfront when they change a product's recipe."

She added: "Skimpflation - quietly changing ingredients to cut costs - has become increasingly common, but it can feel particularly sneaky as shoppers may not realise a product has changed until they get it home and eat it."

News.title: Oscar-winning film producer Jeremy Thomas dies aged 77
News.content:
Oscar-winning producer Jeremy Thomas, whose films included The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, has died aged 77.

The British filmmaker "passed away peacefully" surrounded by family and loved ones at his home in Oxfordshire on Friday, his publicist said in a statement.

Thomas built an international reputation over a career spanning five decades, working with directors including David Cronenberg, Nagisa Oshima, Julien Temple and Nicolas Roeg and backing independent films alongside mainstream successes.

His best known work, Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor, won nine Academy Awards, including best picture, and earned Thomas an Oscar as producer in 1988.

The critically-acclaimed biographical drama about the final monarch of China's Qing dynasty starred Joan Chen, Peter O'Toole and Vivian Wu.

Thomas repeatedly collaborated with Bertolucci, also producing The Sheltering Sky, Little Buddha, Stealing Beauty and The Dreamers.

He also collaborated with several British directors at the start of their careers including Ben Wheatley, Jonathan Glazer, Stephen Frears and David Mackenzie.

Thomas's other credits include Oshima's Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence, starring David Bowie, Cronenberg's A Dangerous Method, Roeg's Bad Timing and Eureka, Fast Food Nation, The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle, and the film adaptations of the JG Ballard books Crash and High-Rise.

After beginning as a film editor, London-based Thomas landed his first production role on the 1976 Australian film Mad Dog Morgan.

In 2006 he received the European Film Academy's award for Outstanding European Achievement in World Cinema and in 2009 was made a CBE in the New Year Honours.

Thomas's latest collaboration with Japanese director Takashi Miike, Bad Lieutenant:Tokyo, is due to premiere at the Toronto Film Festival on Monday.

News.title: Elderly woman found dead named by police
News.content:
An elderly woman whose death sparked a murder investigation has been named by police.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) said Jill Gant, aged 88, was found dead at an address on Appleford Drive in Abingdon, Oxfordshire at about 14:20 BST on Thursday afternoon.

Her family are being supported by specially trained officers.

A 36-year-old man from Abingdon who was arrested on suspicion of murder remains in police custody.

News.title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK
News.content:
A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.

Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.

"Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.

"There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.

News.title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm
News.content:
Six people have been rescued after a 46ft yacht got into difficulty off the coast of Northern Ireland.

Red Bay Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) spent seven hours at sea in the early hours of Saturday morning off Cushendall, County Antrim.

Belfast Coastguard received a distress call from the boat, which had been travelling from Oban in Scotland to Portugal.

The yacht lost all power and steering after making contact with a fish farm in Red Bay, in 60 knots of wind, causing it to become trapped.

A lifeboat was launched at 03:22 BST, with an inshore lifeboat also launched.

In a statement Red Bay RNLI described the weather conditions as "difficult" due to "Force 9 gusting winds, driving rain and the darkness of night".

The RNLI crew observed that those on the yacht were safe and, given the difficult weather and sea conditions, the decision was made "for the sailors to remain onboard the yacht and for the lifeboat to standby until daylight broke" at 07:30.

At 09.30 the lifeboat crew "successfully freed the yacht from the fish farm and brought the sailors safely to Glenarm".

Those on the yacht stayed onboard the vessel while it was towed by the RNLI, who said there were no injuries.

The yacht is now receiving repairs.

Speaking following the call out, Paddy McLaughlin, Red Bay RNLI Coxswain said: "This was a challenging call out in difficult weather conditions, but we were delighted to bring the sailors to safety, and we would like to wish them well.

"We would also like to commend our colleagues in the Coastguard and thank our crew who responded quickly in the middle of the night, launched our lifeboats in darkness and made their way to the scene in what were gale force conditions, and for then spending seven hours at sea."

News.title: Four arrested during gangland violence 'day of action'
News.content:
Police have arrested four men during a pre-planned "day of action" as part of an ongoing investigation into gangland violence.

Police executed warrants at addresses in Bellshill and Motherwell on Friday and also recovered four stolen vehicles.

One of the men arrested, a 29-year-old, was charged after a car crashed into a house in Eaglesham on Friday 21 August. There were no reports of any injuries. He is due to appear in court on Monday.

It brings the total number of arrests as part of Operation Portaledge to 81.

News.title: Driver threatened with knife as bus hijacked and chased in police pursuit
News.content:
A man has been arrested after a hijacked bus was brought to a stop after a police chase.

The driver of the bus was threatened at knife point by a man, who then allowed passengers to leave the bus. However, the bus driver was kept on board.

Videos circulating on social media appear to show a Translink Goldliner coach being driven at speed through residential streets while being chased by a Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) patrol car.

Police said the bus was hijacked in the Beltany Road area of Omagh, Co Tyrone, shortly before 13:00 BST on Saturday.

The man who hijacked the bus then made off in the direction of Newtownstewart and a pursuit ensued along the A5 through Victoria Bridge and Sion Mills. The pursuit lasted nearly 20 miles.

"The bus was eventually stopped in the Head of the Town area of Strabane and a man, aged in his 30s was removed from the bus and subsequently arrested," said a PSNI spokesperson.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) said two people were taken to South West Acute Hospital for treatment.

The NIAS added that they had dispatched two "emergency crews to the incident" and had initially treated to two patients "at the scene".

A number of reports of collisions involving the stolen bus and other vehicles, including a police car and damage to property have been received by police, who are appealing for information.

The Fountain Street and Drumallagh areas in Strabane remain closed at this time and the public are asked to avoid the area.

Sinn FÃ©in councillor Brian Barney Harte said a wall was damaged at the side of a house in Strabane during the pursuit.

He said people were shocked and distressed, adding that his thoughts were with those involved.

"How there has not been a fatality is only by a miracle," he said.

"Numerous cars and properties have been damaged and people have told me of near misses of pedestrians, some pushing prams."

Barney said the bus came to a stop right beside a children's play park and that a police helicopter was involved in the chase.

A spokesperson for public transport operator Translink NI said: "We can confirm an incident occurred involving a Goldliner coach travelling on the Beltany Road in Omagh this afternoon.

"We are assisting the PSNI with their investigation including use of onboard CCTV and would ask anyone with information relating to the incident to contact the police."

News.title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying
News.content:
MPs have voted against proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.

Following a debate in which both sides made emotional speeches, the House of Commons voted 286 to 270 - a majority of 16 - against the proposed legislation.

The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill would have allowed adults with fewer than six months to live to apply to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

A similar bill in the last parliamentary session was supported by MPs before stalling in the House of Lords. The decision from MPs on Friday rules out the prospect of changes to the law on assisted dying in the short term.

The bill tabled by Labour MP Lauren Edwards will make no further progress, although MPs and peers could make another attempt in the next parliamentary session.

Assisted dying is an issue that has been debated for hundreds of hours in Parliament over the last two years and would have represented one of the biggest societal changes in recent years had it been approved.

MPs were given a free vote, meaning they were not required to vote along party lines.

Safeguards within the bill included a requirement that a person applying for an assisted death had the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.

But critics said it included too few measures to protect vulnerable people from being coerced into ending their lives, while some say improving palliative care should be the priority.

News.title: South Africa v New Zealand LIVE: Latest updates as Springboks and All Blacks battle in Baltimore
News.content:
( Getty )

South Africa and New Zealand conclude a thrilling four-Test series with one last meeting in the novel surroundings of Baltimore.

The Springboks took an unassailable 2-1 lead in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series with success in the last encounter on South African soil last week, and the world champions will seek to make another statement here. A strong side has been named by Rassie Erasmus as he looks to avoid a drawn series – with the All Blacks sure to be highly charged after consecutive defeats and the loss of captain Ardie Savea to a shoulder injury.

This clash takes place at the home of the NFL’s Baltimore Ravens, and takes place in the USA in the name of rugby’s global expansion. With two World Cup Stateside on the horizon in the men’s and women’s game, this is another useful staging post for the sport as it looks to build fans and showcase its thrills and spills – and what better fixture to do exactly that?

News.title: Sunderland v Arsenal LIVE: Latest score and updates as Premier League champions bid to continue unbeaten start
News.content:
( Reuters )

Sunderland will hope to give Arsenal another tricky test at the Stadium of Light as the Premier League champions aim to extend their impressive start to their title defence.

The Gunners saw an 11-match winning run come to an end in dramatic fashion in a 2-2 draw at Sunderland last season but have started this campaign in flying form, with Martin Odegaard securing all three points against Napoli in the Champions League in midweek.

The Black Cats will aim to continue a decent start to their sophomore top-flight season, having beaten Fulham 1-0 and drawn with Brentford after a surprise defeat to Ipswich in the first game of the campaign.

Sunderland have not beaten Arsenal in their last 17 attempts but former Gunners captain Granit Xhaka continues to be the driving force at the Stadium of Light and he will hope to make life uncomfortable for his former side once again.

Keely Hodgkinson settled for second in a hotly-anticipated women’s 800 metres World Athletics Ultimate Championship final won by her Swiss nemesis Audrey Werro.

One of the most exciting storylines of the 2026 season has been the emergence of a generational women’s 800m field, led by Hodgkinson, European champion Werro and Dutch former hurdler Femke Broeders-Bol, who announced last year she would be focusing on the 800m.

The trio delivered on Saturday night in Budapest, where Werro got out in front early and held off a home straight kick from the Briton to claim $150,000 (£110,828) in prize money, crossing the line in one minute 55.88 seconds.

open image in gallery Audrey Werro claimed another major title ( AP )

Olympic champion Hodgkinson, who claimed £55,415 as the runner-up, finished in 1min 56.26secs, and Broeders-Bol third, 0.48s further back.

Hodgkinson’s training partner Georgia Hunter Bell was the runner-up in a women’s 1500m final won by Poland’s Diamond League champion Klaudia Kazimierska.

The British Olympic bronze medallist was bidding for a fourth major title in 2026 after winning Commonwealth 800m and European 1500m gold as well as the world indoor 1500m title, but she came up just 0.17 short, crossing the line in 3:57:72.

It was a reversal of last month’s European podium in Birmingham, where the Briton beat the Pole, who set a world-leading 3:54.05 at the Diamond League earlier this month.

open image in gallery Klaudia Kazimierska got revenge on Georgia Hunter Bell ( PA )

Hunter Bell still pocketed £55,414 in prize money for finishing second in her 20th race of the season.

Hunter Bell found herself a bit bunched in but managed to break free just before the bend at the end of the back straight on the final lap and battled Kazimierska all the way to the finish.

Earlier, Matthew Hudson-Smith finished fifth in a 400m final won by Botswana’s Collen Kebinatshipi in a national record 43.39.

Max Burgin and Ben Pattison bowed out after the 800m semi-finals, but Ireland’s Mark English, who won an historic European title last month in Birmingham, booked a place in Sunday’s final.

Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu both ducked out of a 100m semi won by world champion Oblique Seville.

The Jamaican was the fastest of the semi-finalists in 9.90. Three other men – the United States’ Kenny Bednarek and Christian Coleman, as well as Botswana’s Olympic 200m champion Letsile Tebogo – all qualified with sub-10 second times.

The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships begin in Budapest across three action-packed days and the men’s 1500m battle, including rivals Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Josh Kerr, is expected to be among the highlights alongside Keely Hodgkinson’s latest battle with Audrey Werro in the women’s 800m.

The new competition, which will bring the top level 2026 track season to a close, sees most of the sport’s biggest names face off across three days of action in the Hungarian capital and there is significant prize money up for grabs.

In Friday’s opening session Hodgkinson, Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol all made smooth progress into the 800m final, while Ingebrigtsen stormed to a stunning win in the 5000m to add to the hype around the 1500m clash.

Here is everything you need to know about the competition.

What is the World Athletics Ultimate Championships?

It is a new concept intended to fill the void in non-Olympic or World Championship years, designed to pit the biggest names against each other for what World Athletics have said is the biggest prize pot in track and field.

What is the format?

The idea is to make it fast-paced and action-packed to keep viewers engaged.

Two semi-finals in the 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 100m hurdles/110m hurdles and 400m hurdles will feature eight athletes and the top four in each will make it through to the final. The 1500m, 5000m and relays will be straight finals.

All field events will be straight finals. World Athletics say that the horizontal jumps and throws will feature four rounds, with each of the eight athletes guaranteed two attempts.

Hodgkinson qualifies as the reigning Olympic champion. ( PA )

When does the competition take place?

The event will be spread across three days at Budapest's National Athletics Centre and will run from Friday 11 September Sunday 13 with three-hour sessions each evening.

If part of the challenge for Andoni Iraola when he took the Liverpool job was mastering the art of winning Premier League games after midweek Champions League dates, he failed his first test. An Anfield afternoon against a side with the wrong sort of 100 percent record ought to have been the ideal introduction to such assignments.

Instead, Fulham got their first point of the season. A Spanish manager with a playing career at right-back had much to savour; but it was Alvaro Arbeloa, not Iraola. A terrific defender under Rafa Benitez, Arbeloa contributed to many a clean sheet in his time at Liverpool. Now Fulham have a first in the Premier League in his reign. Having conceded three goals to left wing-backs against Crystal Palace last week, they conceded none to Liverpool’s three £100m men.

open image in gallery Alvaro Arbeloa could celebrate a first point in the Premier League with Fulham ( Getty )

“Happy with the point and more happy with the performance,” said Arbeloa. “We were more balanced today. We defended so well.” He had made the bold decision to give the Austrian centre-back David Affengruber a debut at Anfield. “He proved how good he is,” Arbeloa said.

But Iraola’s side delivered a disjointed display, failing to touch the heights they reached in their comeback against Atletico Madrid and failing to score for the first time under him. “What was lacking was quite clear. It is the first game we had problems to create chances and score goals,” he admitted.

open image in gallery Liverpool produced a disjointed display ( Reuters )

Their busy week was a factor but, Iraola insisted, it cannot be an excuse. “It is easy [to say] the players were tired, there is a lack of freshness and we cannot hide it,” said Iraola. “It is the worst turnaround in terms of 60 or 70 hours [between games] but this is going to happen in the season and we have to adapt.” Liverpool did not.

If the workload was new for the head coach, the outcome was familiar for both him and Liverpool. They have drawn their first two league games at Anfield under Iraola, and they drew their last two under Arne Slot as well; meet the new boss, same as the old boss?

Probably not, but remarkably Iraola has drawn half of his last 42 league matches. The concerning element for Liverpool is that all three of late, against Newcastle, Nottingham Forest and now Fulham, came against bottom half finishers last season.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola will be concerned about a run of draws ( PA Wire )

Some issues predate Iraola but Liverpool have only won four league games at Anfield in 2026. Some issues are new to Iraola and his first attempt at squad rotation could scarcely be deemed a success. He made three changes but Kostas Tsimikas, one of those he brought in, was hooked at half-time after looking hapless and the other two, Victor Munoz and Ryan Gravenberch, did not make it until the hour. It lends itself to the interpretation that Liverpool’s squad is simply not strong enough, despite the £670m outlay in the last 16 months.

Only one moment hinted at vindication for a spending spree. Alexander Isak dragged a shot just wide from Bradley Barcola’s pass, men with a combined cost that could reach £248m almost combining to deadly effect.

open image in gallery Bradley Barcola was underwhelming on his second start ( Reuters )

Otherwise, Barcola was largely underwhelming on his second start since his £106m move, though it came in his preferred position on the left. Florian Wirtz’s search for his first goal of the season continues and he scuffed a shot. Isak was twice denied by Bernd Leno, once after gliding past a couple of defenders, and glanced a close-range header wide in injury-time but made less of an impression than Fulham’s striking signing, the purposeful Gonzalo Garcia. Similarly, Liverpool’s flair players were outshone by Fulham’s Josh King, exuding promise with lovely footwork and a shot Alisson clawed away.

King and Garcia were both denied in the incident when Liverpool almost gifted Fulham a lead. They were doubly fortunate after Alisson’s horribly misjudged pass to a marked Gravenberch; first the goalkeeper escaped conceding a penalty when he flew in on King and then Jeremy Jacquet came to his rescue by clearing Garcia’s shot off the line. Alisson held his hand up in contrition.

It nevertheless summed up Liverpool’s sloppiness. It was far from their only misplaced pass; one picked out referee Thomas Bramall. As Fulham ended with more shots on target and touches of the ball in the opposition’s box, Liverpool created far too little. When they came closest, it was from a corner, taken by Dominik Szoboszlai and met by the diminutive Munoz, who headed against the bar.

open image in gallery Fulham held firm for a point at Anfield ( Getty )

“It is these kind of games that you need to win sometimes with a set play or a moment of brilliance,” said Iraola. A set-piece almost sufficed but Liverpool’s brilliance came with Alexis Mac Allister’s winner against Atletico on Wednesday. This was altogether more mundane from them.

News.content:

Jamie Redknapp labelled his former club Tottenham Hotspur “diabolical” after their goalless start to the Premier League season continued in a 0-0 draw with Everton.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are yet to register in four top-flight matches, the first time such an ignominious run has occurred to open a campaign in their history.

Spurs began brightly at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but could not consistently trouble Jordan Pickford thereafter in the first goalless draw to have been held at the ground.

The hosts’ troubles in front of goal followed a summer of heavy investment, with new signings including Savio, Omar Marmoush, Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali all unable to make a breakthrough.

And Redknapp was not at all impressed by a performance that saw Spurs booed off.

"After spending £300m, I didn't think there would be a problem scoring goals,” Redknapp said on Sky Sports. “I thought that they might struggle to win games, a few teething problems, but I thought with the players they’ve got in midfield…surely they have goals in this team.

“To not score in the Premier League in six hours of football is absolutely diabolical, whatever way you look at it. They defended better today, the centre-backs were better than what they had been. But there was just not enough. How can you not score in six hours of football?

"They have not got the right balance in the team. There are so many problems to solve in a game just to score a goal."

It leaves Tottenham in the familiar position of 17th – where they have ended the last two Premier League seasons. Everton sit seventh, level on points with cross-city rivals Liverpool.

News.content:

Joe Root admits the England side descended into “chaos” before he returned as Test captain but believes things are back on track after sealing a series whitewash over Pakistan.

Root, who previously served as skipper for five years before standing down in 2022, answered his country’s call after the dramatic retirement of Ben Stokes in June.

Stokes announced his shock departure midway through the Trent Bridge decider against New Zealand, having been stood down from the previous match following a disciplinary probe into a nightclub trip with team-mate Gus Atkinson.

Joe Root admits the England side descended into “chaos” before he returned as Test captain but believes things are back on track after sealing a series whitewash over Pakistan.

Head coach Brendon McCullum was subsequently stripped of his red-ball responsibilities, briefly leaving the Test side with a worrying leadership vacuum.

But Root’s return, in concert with interim head coach Marcus Trescothick, has brought a hat-trick of comfortable wins at Headingley, Lord’s and now Edgbaston, steadying the ship ahead of Stephen Fleming’s arrival as McCullum’s long-term successor.

The Kiwi is due to arrive in the country in the coming days and Root believes he will find a team that has put its turbulent recent past to one side.

“There’s been a lot of chaos around this series before a ball was bowled,” he said after hitting 62 not in Saturday’s eight-wicket win.

“I think the way we’ve handled it on and off the field, the way everyone understands what is expected of them – both as a player and how we want to carry ourselves – is a really good thing.

open image in gallery Root (left) returned as England captain following Ben Stokes’ sudden retirement (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Wire )

“It’s been a very unusual summer, hasn’t it? There’s been a lot of different things happen. We had a resignation mid-series, there has been a few off-field incidents and we’ve got a new coach. Whether you call it chaos, whether you call it unusual, whether you call it unsettling, all of those are fair.

“But ultimately, the thing that I care about and the most important thing is what happens from that. I think the way that we’ve responded to that has been excellent. And the fact that there’s now clarity in what is expected of the group moving forward is quite evident. We build on that now.”

Root had only been back in the saddle a matter of days when another alcohol-related incident hit the headlines, with Brydon Carse arrested and later de-arrested outside a Derby nightspot in events that remain under investigation.

He was removed from the squad and has not been picked since, with Root laying down the law about the standards of behaviour he expected from a group that had attracted criticism for being unprofessional.

“When you’re trying to build a culture it doesn’t happen overnight and it doesn’t happen over the course of three or four weeks,” Root reflected.

“It’s going to take time to keep working at that, living it day in and day out, and that’s something we’ll continue to keep working at. We’ve made some really good strides in the right direction.

open image in gallery Root and Jordan Cox led England to victory at Edgbaston (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“We’ve just got to keep doing the right things and if we can align that with playing well and winning series then everything is heading in the right direction.”

Pakistan finally put England under some pressure in Birmingham after flaccid efforts in the first two games.

A stunning cameo from debutant Razaullah left the hosts chasing 130 and two Mohammad Abbas wickets in the first over of the chase caused some jitters before Root and Jordan Cox eased to the line.

“We’ll be better for it, we’ll learn from it and be prepared next time around,” Root said.

“You learn a lot about your team in those kind of situations.”

News.title: Chelsea’s ‘soft’ problem is becoming impossible for Xabi Alonso’s luxury attack to solve
News.content:

In the end, Chelsea clung on for a brave point. Emiliano Martinez made an important late save. They survived a barrage of set-pieces. And when Cole Palmer stood over a free-kick 30 yards from goal, with the last kick of the game, he pumped it into the stands just to be safe. A draw against a team who were, for much of the afternoon, top of the league? You have to take it.

Of course that wasn’t quite the mood at Stamford Bridge when the final whistle blew on this 2-2 draw. A volley of boos rang out and it was hard to know exactly who they were for. The players, perhaps, who were collectively disconnected and at times individually calamitous. The referee, Farai Hallam, who at one point intercepted a Chelsea counterattack with his feet and picked up the ball with his hands, like a schoolteacher at the end of break time. Chelsea were exasperated when he waved away several handball shouts.

But really it was an outpouring of frustration, that as talented a front three as Chelsea possess, they cannot possibly outscore a defence as chaotic and porous as this one. Chelsea have conceded at least two goals in all four Premier League games this season, 13 goals in six games in all competitions, and that is too much for Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers to overcome every weekend. Arsenal, by comparison, have conceded only once.

Chelsea went from 1-0 up to 2-1 down in six minutes, and Xabi Alonso accused his players of “soft” defending. “We are attacking better than defending,” he understated. “It’s just four games, but the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it, and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls – this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

open image in gallery Hull players celebrate after equalising at Stamford Bridge ( Getty )

Perhaps there was also some confusion mixed into the fans’ outpouring, after a game when Alonso’s team didn’t always make sense. Why was Maxence Lacroix not at the heart of defence from the start? Why doesn’t the manager trust Estevao Willian when Chelsea are chasing a game? What exactly is the purpose of Malo Gusto?

The first Hull goal was particularly troubling from Chelsea’s perspective. Wesley Fofana watched a long ball fly over his head, Gusto lost a 50-50 in the corner and Jorrel Hato lost his senses, misjudging the flight of the cross like it was his first time encountering this strange bouncing sphere. Mohamed Belloumi couldn’t believe his luck as the ball hopped over Hato, and he took the opportunity beautifully with a low drive under Martinez’s body.

Moments before Hull’s second, it was quite obvious to everyone in the stadium before the corner was taken that Belloumi was alone in a sunny glade on the edge of the box. He pleaded for a pass which didn’t come, and yet still had no Chelsea player near him by the time the ball flew into the middle, bounced off the bar and rolled out to his feet. This time his finish took a couple of fortunate deflections, but you couldn’t say Hull deserved any less.

Martinez did not have his finest afternoon. He flapped at the corner which led to Belloumi’s second goal, and in the second half fumbled a routine shot which almost presented the ball to Oli McBurnie to tap in what would have most probably been the winner.

open image in gallery Emiliano Martinez had some unconvincing moments in Chelsea’s goal ( Reuters )

Another recruit from Aston Villa with improvements to make is Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s hirsute set-piece coach, who bobbed around the technical area waving his arms and looking generally exasperated with players who apparently weren’t following his instructions, as if somehow that wasn’t his fault. Some of Chelsea’s intricate attacking corners almost worked, when Palmer would ghost to the front post and receive a low pass, but they need to spend time on the defensive side.

These are early days, of course. Alonso is still learning his best combinations. Chelsea will be better when Moises Caicedo returns, when Marco Palestra finally begins his career here. But for all their successful trading, earning a billion pounds in sales since BlueCo took over, there was a sense that some past players were missing. Trevoh Chalobah, for example, was Chelsea’s best defender for large parts of last season and would surely have enhanced this ragged display.

The only positive is that their attack continues to fire. Rogers and Pedro produced clinical finishes in each half, and while it wasn’t Palmer’s best game, he played a major hand in both goals. Palmer has a habit of drifting to the fringes when it becomes congested, partly out of an instinctive feeling of where the space is, where the opponents’ soft spots are, and partly out of frustration at a lack of involvement. He loitered on the left and then drove into the box to feed Pedro, who lashed a first-time finish into the roof of the net.

open image in gallery Joao Pedro celebrates after levelling for Chelsea in the second half ( Reuters )

But they could not find another, and if anything it was Hull who looked most likely to score a third. No Premier League team have been involved in as many goals as Chelsea so far this season, but Alonso would much rather they were not the top flight’s great entertainers.

“I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we won,” he said. “For sure, it’s some repeated patterns that we are making. It will take time to fix them. When we get the lead, you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back.

“Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances … It was from a long ball, two bounces. The way it happened, you need to be very, very aware, and very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished.”

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history gone four games without scoring a goal from the start of the league season. One can say with confidence that no team has done the same having spent £329m on new players in the preceding summer, and there is still a chance Spurs could reach October without breaking the streak.

They have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa – and once again it feels like a must-watch. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them. A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net profit.

The problem has become acute so early this season that Roberto De Zerbi already finds himself in a difficult place. He might be glad that the home crowd stayed with his team as long as they did. At the end the Spurs manager could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed with it.

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

News.title: Lando Norris on pole for Spanish GP but adds voice to critics of ‘Madring’
News.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen predicted that overtaking would be “practically impossible” in the race. “[The Madring] has a tendency of maybe creating some big shunts in some places,” the Dutchman said. “It reminds me a little bit of Jeddah in a way – fast corners and the walls being very close.

“The only thing that’s already a bit disappointing is that many of the braking zones are angled. This means it’s practically impossible to attack a competitor because you’re braking and simultaneously turning right or left. And that’s the worst thing you can do if you want to create an overtaking opportunity.”

Norris agreed with Verstappen that it would be very difficult to overtake, although that is no bad thing for him provided he can hang on to the lead at the start.

The Briton, though, described the decision to build what is now the longest pit lane on the F1 calendar as a big disappointment.

“I think it has a lot of potential,” Norris said of the Madring. “Just certain things need to be improved. Like the pit lane, which is like six kilometres long. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and the biggest pit loss of the year [in terms of the time it will take to pit – an estimated 25 seconds]. So that just makes overtaking worse. Not overtaking, but it makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse.

“You know, if we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money in building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, is you have a short pit lane so people can pit and you then create overtaking.”

Norris described his pole lap as “one of the best laps of his career” and his team principal Andrea Stella fully agreed, describing it as “a masterpiece”.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player-of-the-match Abi Burton’s first-half score.

Moloney-MacDonald’s try wide out on the left was a show-stopper for the crowd of 9,251 in the North West and demonstrated that England have style to go with solidity. But it was the power game that did for Australia.

The Wallaroos scored tries of their own through Faliki Pohiva and Eva Karpani but spent the vast majority of the game manning the defensive barricades. They did so admirably for 40 minutes but when the dam wall blew it blew spectacularly.

They did not help themselves with sin-binnings in either half for Samantha Wood and Karpani, but over 80 minutes the odds will always be stacked in favour of the full-time side against the part-timers.

“The reality is that even at our best we’re probably not good enough. We will be,” said Tim Walsh, Rugby Australia’s director of women’s high performance. “We need an environment where they can concentrate on being full-time athletes. That’s the vision Rugby Australia have and that’s where we’re headed.”

The game was England’s first with the smaller ball being trialled in the women’s game by World Rugby and they only converted four of their eight tries, a statistic which may be seized upon by those who do not care for it. A rugby pitch is not a sterile laboratory though and the swirling, blustery conditions should be taken into account in any dissection of its value.

Referee: A Groizeleau (France).

News.title: Jordan Cox looks a Joe Root clone as pair steer England home
News.content:
There is perhaps no batsman in Test history as accustomed as Joe Root to walking in with the scoreboard reading “not many for two” and his team in a tight spot.

That is where Root found himself once again soon after 11am on Saturday. His team were two for two, with both openers out for ducks, and the problems of the third evening bleeding into the fourth morning. A chaotic and patchwork Pakistan team suddenly believed Mohammad Abbas could inspire their defence of 130.

A familiar position for Root, sure, but not the young man at the other end, the rookie No 3 Jordan Cox. Together, they eased England out of a creeping crisis with such aplomb that the target was chased swiftly enough that the few thousand at Edgbaston were refunded 50 per cent of their ticket prices because so few overs were bowled. When Cox hit the winning run, a scrambled single into the off side, Root’s relief was palpable. His team had been tested, and he felt they would be “better for it”.

They had won his first series since returning to the captaincy 3-0, but not without a scare at the last. The scorecard will record this as a routine England eight-wicket win and, for the most part, it was. But England were rattled by Razaullah, a 21-year-old who spent the first two Tests of this series in Mardan, in the mountains of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region near Pakistan’s border with Afghanistan. Having bowled quickly, he wreaked havoc on the third evening with his 63-ball 81, taking England from the brink of an innings victory to an awkward chase.

Razaullah’s partner with the bat was Abbas, who provided England with an almighty fright on the fourth morning. First ball, Ben Duckett was caught behind. The ball was angled in, demanding that it was played, then nipped slightly away, taking the edge. Duckett’s trudge off was glacial, with his curious Test summer over. He has scored England’s only century of the season, but failed to make fifty otherwise. In this series, he has averaged just eight.

News.title: Razaullah’s incredible hitting scrambles England’s minds
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Badenoch must scrap triple lock, says senior Tory MP | Politician urges Conservatives to ‘slaughter some sacred cows’ to stabilise the public finances

2) | Michael O’Leary demands sacking of ‘incompetent’ air traffic control chief | Ryanair boss urges Transport Secretary to dismiss Martin Rolfe after IT meltdown grounds passengers

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

Alexander the Great

Liverpool’s Swedish striker had a torrid time with injuries in his first season at Anfield, but the fit-again forward has started the season on fire with three goals in as many games. Sports.title: Tottenham 0 Everton 0: Spurs STILL yet to score in Premier League despite £300million rebuild amid another poor showing
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM continued to fire blanks as they barron run in the Premier League continued against Everton.

Spurs hosted the Merseysiders hoping to kickstart their Premier League campaign.



Neither side could find the breakthrough goal in the first 45 minutes at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Spurs’ frustrations in front of goal continued as they were unable to find the target with a single shot in the first half.



Antonín Kinsky almost gave away the opening goal in the 65th minute but Kieran Dewsbury-Hall could not take advantage of the poor pass out.

It was Brennan Johnson who then spurned a great chance for the visitors as he sliced his shot on his return to North London.



Lucas Bergvall almost broke the deadlock in the 89th minute, but his curling effort was tipped behind by Jordon Pickford.

MORE TO FOLLOW…

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy’s Burnley debut overshadowed by goalkeeping howler with Clarets rock bottom of Championship
Sports.content:
JAMIE VARDY’s Burnley debut was derailed after a goalkeeping disaster kicked off a nightmare afternoon for the Clarets.

Leicester legend Vardy returned to English football earlier this month for the first time since leaving the Foxes in favour of Serie A side Cremonese.



But his homecoming was far from smooth sailing, thanks in part to a calamitous bit of goalkeeping from young stopper Max Weiss.

The German youth international joined in a reported £4.3million deal from Karlsruher in 2025, and has been promoted to first choice keeper so far this season.



But that status could come under threat after he gifted Swansea an opener after just 14 minutes on Saturday.

Weiss was given an age to clear up an overhit long ball from opposition keeper Lawrence Vigouroux, with Irish international Adam Idah chasing the ball down from a mile away.



But for some reason, Weiss, 22, decided to take a risky touch rather than clearing the ball to safety.

The poor touch popped the ball into the air, where he tried to pass it to his defender – but by that point Idah had closed down the gap and stole the ball off Weiss’ toes before finishing into an empty net.

One fan wrote of the moment: “It’s absolutely embarrassing, he’s probably a lovely lad but he’s an awful goalkeeper Get him off immediately.”

While another harshly added: “Worst goalkeeping performance I’ve seen in Swansea in years.”

Moussa Yeo added a second Swans goal in the 33rd minute before summer arrival Largie Ramazani pulled one back in the second half.

Vardy was finally called upon in the 65th minute, being introduced up front in place of midfielder Ugo Raghouber in hopes of a later equaliser.

But Championship golden boot winner Zan Vipotnik outran Kyle Walker at the back post to add the finishing touches for Swansea three minutes later, sealing three points for the Welsh side.

The loss left Nicky Hayen’s side rock bottom of the Championship table, and one of just two sides in the division yet to record a win.



Their 16 goals against is the worst defensive record in the division, and their eight goals at the other end of the pitch is nothing to write home about.

At this rate Vardy could be in for a reunion of sorts with former club Leicester, who are currently languishing in the mid-table of League One.

Sports.title: Chelsea wonderkid Reggie Watson steals the show as U21s thump talented Arsenal squad featuring Max Dowman
Sports.content:
CHELSEA might not have been able to beat Arsenal when it mattered most, but their Under-21s exacted some form of revenge on the Gunners when they met on Saturday.

It was a talented young Arsenal side too, which featured the highly-rated Marli Salmon and wonderkid Max Dowman.



But the young Blues have their own crop of exciting talent, with Cole Palmer‘s pal Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli featuring alongside Reggie Watson, who started against Leeds in the Carabao Cup just a few days ago.

And they boast a good record against their London rivals, having beaten them four times and only losing twice in the Premier League 2 – with no defeats in the last four meetings.



And Chelsea duly ran out 4-1 victors away from home on Saturday lunchtime.

Emulating the shape played by the first team – a three at the back system – it was right wing-back Leo Black who opened the scoring after 14 minutes.



And with Chelsea leading it was time for the star of the show to step up – Watson.

The 16-year-old midfielder was hooked at half-time in the Carabao Cup win over Leeds, but he didn’t play badly and became Chelsea’s fourth youngest player in history in the process.

It might be a case of too good for the U21’s and not quite ready for the first team.

He scored a brace, one of which was a penalty, to put his side three goals to the good with 72 minutes played.



But it was all about his second, a free-kick which is becoming his trademark.

With a wall placed to cover the left side of the goal, Watson whipped a powerful free-kick to the side of which the keeper was standing on, completely evading the wall and catching the stopper by surprise to add Chelsea’s third.

James Scanlon, formerly of Manchester United, got the Gunners a goal back with 11 minutes to play, but it was too little, too late.

With last season’s PL2 Player of the Season Shim Mheuka now on loan at Celtic, his CNG replacement has been stepping up of late.

Chizzy Ezenwata spent last season thriving with the U18s, and has now made the step up to play for the U21s, taking his promotion in his stride.



The 18-year-old bagged the last goal of the game, having also scored in their 5-4 thriller over West Ham last time out.

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Paul Scholes watch on in away end as Salford in six-goal thriller with red card
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE and Paul Scholes were in the away end as Salford City played out a six-goal thriller.

The Ammies were away at Rotherham for their League Two clash at the AESSEAL New York Stadium.



The Manchester United legends were treated to an exciting 90 minutes of EFL action.

Salford took an early lead through Ryan Gordon before Joe Powell doubled up in the 31st minute.



The hosts quickly hit back to level the match as Brandon Cover and former Wrexham ace Paul Mullin both found the net.

Ossama Ashley put Rotherham ahead ten minutes into the second half before Macaulay Langstaff converted from the spot to make the score 3-3.



The goal from Ashley would have stung as it was his first since being released by the Ammies earlier this year.

There was further drama as Ibbi Odoh was sent off after appealing for a penalty just minutes before Langstaff scored.

Former England manager and United coach Steve McClaren was also watching on from the posh seats.

Neville and Scholes were part of the original Class of ’92 group – along with Phil Neville, Ryan Giggs and Nicky Butt – who first invested in the club back in 2014.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest star Dan Ndoye left with blood pouring from his nose after accident during Aston Villa clash
Sports.content:
NOTTINGHAM FOREST ace Dan Ndoye was left with a bloody nose during the Premier League clash with Aston Villa following a freak accident.

Ndoye, 25, helped Forest pick up their first victory of the season with a dramatic 2-1 win over Unai Emery’s men at Villa Park.



However, Forest manager Oliver Glasner was left stressing over the winger in the first half when he was on the wrong end of an unfortunate collision.

The Switzerland international caught a stray arm from team-mate Ola Aina in the half-hour mark that left him with blood pouring from his nose.



Ndoye bled so heavily that Forest physios had to immediately replace the patching they initially placed on him.

The forward was able to continue but the cotton wool in both nostrils absorbed an immense amount of blood as the game developed.



The ex-Bologna star came off on 76 minutes when he was replaced by Igor Jesus.

Forest opened the scoring with £50million record signing Liam Delap, who netted his first goal for his new team with a fine finish from distance.

However, Villa hit back and scored their first Premier League goal of the season with summer signing Alysson, who also broke his duck.

But Glasner’s decision to hook Ndoye paid dividends as Jesus, 25, proved to be the hero.

Sports.title: Derby issue update on Henrik Meister after striker collapsed with nobody around him in Birmingham clash
Sports.content:
MEISTER WORRY Derby issue update on Henrik Meister after striker collapsed with nobody around him in Birmingham clash

DERBY have revealed striker Henrik Meister walked out of the stadium unaided after going down off the ball against Birmingham.

The 22-year-old Dane was involved in a clash of heads in the second half of their 2-1 defeat before falling to the turf.



The forward, who is a recent loan signing from Pisa, was treated for seven minutes on the pitch.

He was eventually carried off on a stretcher down the tunnel to a standing ovation by both sets of fans.



Derby have now issued an update on the player and said he was able to leave Pride Park without help despite initial worries over his condition.

A club statement read: “A positive update on Henrik.

“The forward was checked over by the club’s medics after being carried off on a stretcher early in the second half.

“Thankfully, he walked out of the stadium unaided following the final whistle. He will now follow the concussion protocols.”

Boss John Eustace said Meister “seems OK” and confirmed the club would follow concussion protocols.

He added: “To lose him just after half-time was tough. It was difficult, but he’s OK now.



“He’s having concussion protocols. We’ll just have to see how he is. I’ve been speaking to him and he seems OK.”

Meister was making his first home start for John Eustace’s side after being handed his debut in a 3-0 Championship defeat at West Ham last weekend.

The score was level at 1-1 at the time of Meister’s withdrawal.

Bobby Clark had fired the Rams in front on 40 minutes.

But Blues levelled via Carlos Vicente barely two minutes later.



Birmingham boss Chris Davies turned to Paik Seung-ho on the hour mark, replacing Jhon Solis.

And it proved to be an inspired decision, with Paik giving his side the lead just four minutes later.

Paik’s goal was enough to seal all three points for Davies’ men.

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Jorrel Hato hooked after disastrous 45 minutes as Cole Palmer leads Blues’ frightening new attack
Sports.content:
HIGH-FLYING Chelsea were handed a reality check as they were held to a 2-2 draw with Premier League newcomers Hull at Stamford Bridge.

A pair of goals from Mohamed Belloumi equalled strikes from Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro to keep the post-promotion party going in East Yorkshire.



But Chelsea fans will be disappointed with how the result came about, and especially with one defender whose lapse in focus cost the Blues.

They will be able to take some comfort in the knowledge that their young attack is still as lethal as ever.



Here’s how SunSport’s Jack Rosser rated the Blues at Stamford Bridge…

Emiliano Martinez – 5

The Argentine was signed to solve Chelsea’s problems between the sticks, but kept them going here.



Martinez raced out of his goal to try and claim the ball from the corner which led to Belloumi’s second goal of the afternoon, but missed the ball completely.

Chelsea need a consistent performer who the back four can trust in goal, but don’t seem to be there yet.

Malo Gusto – 5

Another rough day for Chelsea’s defence and the Frenchman’s display rather summed it up.

Gusto was popping up all over the back four as well as in midfield at times – seemingly without much of a plan as to what he was doing there.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Gusto always offers plenty of energy, but there was little quality on show against Hull.

Levi Colwill – 6

Far from an eye-catching performance but stepped in at times to clean up some ugly moments at the back when everything was going wrong around him.

A slow start to the season from the academy graduate, but clearly more trusted by Alonso given Maxence Lacroix was dropped to the bench.

Wesley Fofana – 5

Dragged towards the ball a little too much during the first half spell in which Hull stunned the Blues, leaving others exposed.

Tried to get Chelsea going again after the break with some driving runs from the back.



Jorrel Hato – 4

A disastrous first half which led to the youngster being replaced at the break.

Hato was caught under a bouncing ball for Hull’s first goal and dragged all over the place by the Tigers before Alonso made the call to hook him early.

Reece James – 6

Again starting in the midfield two, James was tasked with covering as much ground as possible, to his detriment.



James saw a decent free-kick stopped as well as a low effort from the edge of the box but struggled to control the game from midfield, which led to the back line being exposed.

Romeo Lavia – 5

A rather unremarkable afternoon from the midfielder, who started alongside skipper James in a midfield two.

Neat enough on the ball but not able to cause much trouble going forwards with his passing.

The Blues are seriously missing the presence of Moises Caicedo.

Pedro Neto – 4

Handed a new contract on Friday but followed it up with a very frustrating performance.



The Portugal international was pushed forwards a touch from wing-back to right-wing but did not make any sort of impression or cause the Tigers back line much trouble.

Often a reliable player, but Chelsea have plenty of options to play out wide and performances like that will not help.

Cole Palmer – 7

Palmer was involved in both goals, first finding Pedro from the right in the build up to Rogers’ opener in a move which saw the entire front three combine – before setting up Pedro for the second.



Palmer pushed to make something happen after the break too, popping up in pockets and seeing a shot fizz wide of the far post.

Should have done much better when found in space in the box, only to delay a shot and lift it well over the bar.

Morgan Rogers – 7

Rogers’ fine start to life as the most expensive British player in history continued with a very well taken strike after just seven minutes.

The winger drifted past Regan Slater with ease before catching the keeper out with a powerful effort to the near post on his weaker foot.

Quieter from then on but another decent afternoon for the summer signing.



Joao Pedro – 7

What felt like a slight dip in performance from Pedro still ended with a goal and an assist for the Brazilian.

Alonso compared him to Karim Benzema and talked him up as being as good as Erling Haaland this week, which could well have ended his fine form – but the clever near post finish backed up the hype.

This was not an awe-inspiring display, but so long as the numbers keep ticking up Pedro will be happy.



Substitutes

Pep Chavarria (for Hato 45′) – 6

Settled the left hand side well after Hato’s first half horror show, though the summer signing offered little on the ball.

Loudly booed by the travelling Hull fans, something he will have to get used to playing here after the World Cup, Barco snapped into a few challenges and added a bit of bite to midfield.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich 3: Zian Flemming’s last-gasp winner seals massive win for Tractor Boys vs ten-man Eagles
Sports.content:
ZIAN FLEMMING helped the Tractor Boys reap a three-point harvest in South London as Ipswich beat Crystal Palace 3-2.

Jorgen Strand Larsen looked to have saved Axel Disasi from disaster after his strike put Palace level following the Frenchman’s first-half sending off.



But there was to be no valiant comeback story for Palace as they fell to a defeat against Ipswich at Selhurst Park for the first time since 2010.

With identical records in the league it was no surprise there was nothing to separate these two sides in the opening half an hour, with goals from Anan Khalaili and Emersonn cancelling each other out.



But Disasi’s needless studs up challenge on Jack Clarke in the Ipswich half saw Palace surrender the lead and a chance at successive wins in the Premier League, something they have not done since last December.

Leif Davis had been the provider for the Tractor Boys’ opener before he turned goalscorer for the goal that put Gary O’Neil’s side on course for their first win in the league since the opening day.



Yet a profligate Ipswich display in the second half gave the Eagles enough of a lift to get back into the game despite being down to 10-men, with Strand Larsen’s clinical strike across goal seeing the two sides level entering the 89th minute.

But a Davis header floated towards goal and hit the crossbar before it fell kindly to Flemming, whose shot wrong-footed Benitez to squirm in at the far post and see Ipswich take the three points.

Palace boss Pierre Sage was without Dean Henderson because of an ankle injury he picked up in their Conference League final win against Freiburg.

That saw Sage opt for Walter Benitez between the sticks, marking his first Premier League start since March, while Adam Wharton wore the captain’s armband in Henderson’s place.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The South Londoners were also without their famous Holmesdale Fanatics ultras, the Ipswich clash being the second league game without the group after they effectively disbanded.

But they could have desperately used their voices in support after Disasi’s silly red card – and perhaps an even more damning assessment when the away end started chanting “you’re support is f***ing s***.”

The balance of the clash had been on a knife-edge in the opening quarter of an hour, with neither team able to force a breakthrough.

That was until Yeremy Pino cut through the Ipswich defence like butter to play in Daichi Kamada, who in turn passed the ball to flying right wing-back Khalail who thundered home his first goal for the Eagles.



Palace threatened to grab a second when Jorgen Strand Larsen, fresh off the back of his brace against Middlesbrough midweek, lashed the ball at goal after a great ball in behind by Khalaili.

But his effort went straight at Kjell Scherpen, who parried it away with firm hands.



Ipswich got themselves level pegging again after Emersonn was left unchallenged by the Palace backline, who fell asleep waiting for an offside flag that never arrived.

Emersonn notched his second goal of the season as he headed a wonderful Davis cross past the hapless Benitez 10 minutes after the opener.

Another 10 minutes later, Disasi inexplicably decided he simply had to challenge Clarke – making his first start of the season for the visitors – for a loose ball.

But the 28-year-old was late to the challenge, and was promptly given his marching orders by Chris Kavanagh before VAR Craig Pawson confirmed the decision – with the former Chelsea man standing by the corner flag in front of the players tunnel while he bizarrely waited for confirmation on the stonewall red card.

Sage opted for the conservative approach and switched out Pino for Takehiro Tomiyasu.



And the signs of a goal were there to see when only a poor touch stopped Clarke from shooting from close range, with the ball cleared by Chris Richards.

The breakthrough would come a minute later, with Abdul Fatawu slipping a pass down the side of the Eagles defence for Dara O’Shea, who delivered a ball into Emersonn whose failed attempt at a shot then found Davis in acres of space at the far post.

Ipswich seemed to play with their food for much of the second half, with one occasion seeing Julio Enciso speed in behind Richards to lay a pass to Fatawu who then tried to turn in the area instead of shooting before Palace got back in numbers to defend.



Benitez then produced a smart save to deny Clarke, but it wasn’t until the 68th minute when winds of change in the game started to open the door for a Palace equaliser.

Palace continued to threaten as attack after attack swooped towards the Ipswich box, before Strand Larsen sunk his talons into the goal with his vicious shot across goal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The home fans had also found their voice even without their ultras, drowning out the away support for the final 20 minutes and that was reflected on the pitch with it seeming like it was the visitors who were a man down.

But Flemming’s first Prem goal of the season saw Ipswich escape potential embarrassment by landing all three points.
