Sports.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Big fan of Forty Years On in Sceptre Stakes
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle previews the final day of the St Leger Festival at Doncaster - live on Sky Sports Racing – alongside top-quality action on Champions’ Weekend at The Curragh.

Scott filly can make winning Stakes debut

I've made no secret of my admiration for FORTY YEARS ON who can make an instant impact in Pattern company when she contests the feature race at Doncaster on Sunday, the Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies Stakes (3.05).

George Scott, who won Friday's Doncaster Cup with Caballo De Mar, has found a great opportunity for this most progressive daughter of Mayson who was much too good for her rivals in a valuable handicap at Goodwood last month.

She enjoys ease underfoot and can win for the sixth time in eight starts at the possible expense of Shadwell's Touleen, who brings solid Group One form to the race after her luckless run in the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot.

She did look a bit awkward in the Valiant Stakes last time so the cheekpieces may just sharpen her focus, while Planet Seeker looks over-priced on the strength of her York form and her creditable fourth in the Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

Longer trip ideal for Bailey gelding in Mallard

It's hard to fault SAY WHAT YOU SEE in the Betfred Mallard Handicap (3.40) on Sunday following a string of rock-solid races for his trainer Liam Bailey this year.

He built on a near miss at Southwell with an eye-catching run at York's Ebor Festival, staying on from a long way back to finish a closing third over 12 furlongs and should appreciate this longer trip.

There's probably a nice race in Godolphin's Valedictory who was a little one-paced over two miles at York last time, having looked the real deal earlier in the season with back-to-back wins at Goodwood and Newmarket. He has something to prove off his current mark, however.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Doyle bit back at Sky Sports Racing's Seb Sanders after criticism of his winning ride in the Flying Childers at Doncaster, which saw Final Objective veer across the track and cause a rival to stumble badly

Boughey has strong hand in sprint

I like George Boughey's lightly raced ASUKA in the Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (1.55) on Sunday's Doncaster card.

Dropping back to six furlongs on such a big galloping track shouldn't be an issue for the Night Of Thunder gelding who confirmed himself in top form over further at Chester last time when a poor draw and an interrupted run put paid to his chances.

George has a strong hand in the race with stable mate Oliver Show also bringing some strong form to the table. His run behind subsequent winner Inspired at Goodwood last time reads well and the first-time visor is an interesting angle.

Easier surface a positive for course winner

I'm looking forward to seeing LANGSTONE back on an easier surface in the Betfred City Of Doncaster Handicap (2.30) on Sunday.

Clive Cox's three-year-old broke his maiden over course and distance in the spring before following up on the All-Weather but didn't enjoy the fast ground in the Britannia at Royal Ascot. He hasn't been seen in public since so he arrives on Town Moor much fresher than his rivals and remains well treated off a slightly reduced mark of 92.

Zooming should also appreciate a more sympathetic surface for the first time since winning her maiden at Newmarket last autumn. She has been highly tried this year and drops into handicap company for the first time off what looks a workable mark of 94.

Image: The Sceptre Stakes headlines the final day at Doncaster as the fabulous four-day festival draws to a close

Goddess can have her day in the sun

I can't wait to see how SUN GODDESS performs back at Group One level in the Moyglare Stud Stakes (2.50) at The Curragh on Sunday following her demolition job in a valuable sales race at York last month.

Aidan O'Brien's filly had it all to do after running into trouble on The Knavesmire, but her class prevailed in the end as she ran out a most impressive six-length winner. This is much tougher, of course, as she tackles seven furlongs for the first time on a stiffer track, but I'm confident the Phoenix Stakes winner is up to the task.

Green Empress travelled well when getting off the mark in the Group Two Debutante Stakes over course and distance last month, beating the re-opposing Alpha, Ibelieveicanfly and Dancing Destiny and looks the main danger.

Sandals ready to take a big step forward

The way Starlust hit the line behind US raider Bacio in the Nunthorpe Stakes at York tells me he can run another massive race in the BAR 1 Betting Flying Five Stakes (3.25) at The Curragh.

Ralph Beckett's five-year-old came out of retirement following a fruitless spell at stud and looks to have found the form that won him the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint two years ago.

TIME FOR SANDALS' last two runs have been solid, and I like the way she flashed home in the Nunthorpe after repeatedly finding trouble mid-race. If things fall her way, she could be the one they all have to beat with Kieran Shoemark in the saddle.

Image: Time For Sandals (centre) is Hollie Doyle's pick in the Flying Five

Sequoia can post a giant run in National

Juddmonte colt Monogram looked a class act when scoring over course and distance for Joseph O'Brien and can take the step up to Group One company in his stride in the Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes (4.00).

One thing he does lack, however, is experience which could give GIANT SEQUOIA the advantage. Aidan O'Brien's first string won the Group Two Futurity Stakes here last time and is clearly a colt of huge potential.

On the evidence of that run, the son of the great Frankel is still open to enough improvement to make his presence felt at the very highest level so gets my vote in a mouthwatering renewal.

Brilliant Scandinavia set for fifth Group One

With a seven-race unbeaten streak to his name, I can't wait to see the brilliant SCANDINAVIA enhance his reputation in the Comer Group International Irish St Leger (4.35) on Sunday.

Aidan O'Brien's Gold Cup winner steps back to one mile and six furlongs which shouldn't be a problem on such a stiff track, and he can justify short odds in his quest for a fifth victory at the highest level.

Stable companion Jan Brueghel, who, like Scandinavia is a Doncaster St Leger winner, is the obvious danger. He looked as good as ever when winning this season's Coronation Cup and won't mind this greater test of stamina.

Sports.title: 'No idea what to expect’ – F1 braced for Madring debut race mystery
Sports.content:
George Russell believes Formula 1's first race at the Madring could swing one of two extreme ways, while Lewis Hamilton admits he does not know what exactly to expect, heading into Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix.

The wall-lined circuit in Madrid has proved a big challenge for drivers so far on its inaugural weekend, while Friday's practice running showed up tyre degradation difficulties on long heavier-fuel runs.

The grid's leading drivers are braced for those challenges to continue into a 57-lap race for which McLaren's Lando Norris starts on pole position ahead of Mercedes' championship-leading Kimi Antonelli.

Mercedes' Russell, who qualified sixth after a disappointing Q3, told Sky Sports F1: "I think tyre degradation will define it one way or another.

"There will either be no degradation and it will be a procession, or really high degradation and it will be pretty chaotic."

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who qualified fourth having initially held provisional pole after the first flying laps of Q3, is also expecting tyre management to play a central role.

"We all came into the weekend thinking there would not be much degradation and the tyres would last long but it turns out there was a lot of degradation [on Friday]," said Hamilton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reflects on his Spanish Grand Prix qualifying lap, which saw the Ferrari drive secure fourth.

"I'm sure that will improve as the car gets grippier, but I have no idea what to expect."

And championship leader Antonelli, who was pipped to pole position by a sensational final lap by Norris, predicted: "Probably it's going to be grandmother driving in the first 10 laps, but let's see.

"We saw in the long run how steep the degradation can be, especially if you push too early. We will try to see in the moment.

"Maybe we go into the race and the degradation is going to be much lower."

Image: Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris and Max Verstappen after qualifying in the top three for the Spanish GP

Why Norris is on the 'backfoot' despite pole

It seems track position could be critical, so, in theory, Norris is in the best position as he starts on pole ahead of Antonelli, Verstappen and Hamilton.

But, the McLaren driver missed almost all of second practice on Friday due to a gearbox issue and has not completed any meaningful long running as a consequence.

"I have to do my homework tonight. I'm on the backfoot from a high fuel perspective. I've not done any," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris describes his lap which claimed him Spanish GP pole as one of his best

"I need to use the data we have from Oscar and see what uses I can have, looking at onboard videos and data from everyone.

"Not an ideal situation but I gave myself the best chance and we will prepare the best way possible. Luckily it's not the best track to overtake on, so we will focus on a good start, good lap one and see what we can do."

In Friday's practice sessions, the tyre degradation was extremely high due to the successive high-speed corners, including the big banked 'La Monumental' Turn 12 where the tyres experience high loads.

"Everyone found out there was a lot of graining on the tyres," said McLaren team principal Andrea Stella.

"I'm not sure everyone has clear ideas as to what strategies we have ahead of us, so it will be entertaining."

Is a one-stop race even possible? Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins



“I think hanging it out for a one-stop, if you think of Monaco, you can go slowly, manage the tyres and not get that graining through [the banked] Turn 12. Perhaps you can extend the life of the tyres and make a one-stop work.



“But if overtaking is possible, because of high tyre degradation, you won’t be able to drive slowly enough to make that happen.



"At this stage I see it being a two-stop race and a disruptive race."

How much overtaking will there be?

The pace between the front-runners should be close, so the race is likely going to come down to tyre degradation, which will dictate how much overtaking there is.

Norris is in the best position, as he can control the pace, but if overtaking is possible, he cannot afford to drive too slowly to save his tyres. But that's the big question mark, is there enough room to overtake?

"The only thing you can do is try to put pressure on the car in front, trying to make them make a mistake or make them deg a bit more, and then you try to play with strategy," said Antonelli.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reflects on a 'tricky' Spanish Grand Prix qualifying.

"But, especially when you have a very similar pace, it is difficult to make a move."

The awkward turn five chicane is expected to be the best overtaking spot, but Verstappen feels the curvature of the track means it will even be difficult to attack into that particular corner.

"In some places, in the braking zones, they need to learn that you should never have to steer while braking. You need to be able to combine under braking because otherwise it doesn't allow any kind of overtaking," said the Red Bull driver.

"For sure, in terms of track design, I think it can be better. I also think driver input on track design in the future could help a lot. I know they'll always come back to you and say, 'Yeah, but the space,' but that's BS. There's always a way to create an overtaking opportunity around a track."

Sports.title: Norris beats Antonelli with 'masterpiece' to take Spanish GP pole
Sports.content:
Lando Norris produced a stunning lap to beat Kimi Antonelli to the first pole position at Formula 1's all-new Madring circuit in a thrilling Spanish Grand Prix Qualifying.

The McLaren driver hadn't appeared to be in contention for pole at any point of the session, but found a huge amount of pace on his final run to edge out championship leader Antonelli by 11 thousandths of a second.

Max Verstappen, who had surged into pole contention earlier in the session, edged out Lewis Hamilton for third after the Ferrari driver produced a strong recovery having crashed in final practice earlier on Saturday.

Charles Leclerc starts behind his Ferrari team-mate in fifth, while Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate and nearest championship challenger, George Russell, could only manage sixth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Lando Norris took the Spanish Grand Prix pole with this sensational final lap

The remarkable nature of Norris' lap was further highlighted by a near-half second gap to his team-mate Oscar Piastri in seventh.

Norris said: "I'm shocked! A little bit surprised to be here now. My god, that was probably one of the best laps I've done in my career.

"Very, very happy. Very proud, very happy for the team. Just one of those laps where everything came together.

Spanish GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



6) George Russell, Mercedes



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) Liam Lawson, Red Bull



9) Franco Colapinto, Alpine



10) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls





"I had a good idea of what I wanted to do. It was whether my brain let me do it on the last lap. Everything pretty much worked perfectly."

With overtaking expected to prove difficult around the tight circuit, Norris has given himself a strong chance of claiming a third victory in four races and reducing a 96-point deficit to Antonelli.

Despite losing out to Norris, Antonelli is well positioned to extend his 66-point championship lead over Russell and move closer to a maiden title, with nine rounds remaining after Sunday's race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reflects on a 'tricky' Spanish Grand Prix qualifying.

Red Bull's Liam Lawson, who continues to deputise for the injured Isack Hadjar, was eighth, while Alpine's Franco Colapinto and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

A supreme collective display of driving saw the session pass without any of the red-flag stoppages that had been expected at the hugely challenging new circuit.

Haas driver Oliver Bearman was unable to participate due to the heavy damage done to his car in a big crash in final practice, but there were only kisses rather than heavy contact with the barriers as the field pushed to the limit in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Bearman took a huge hit right at the end of P3 at the Spanish Grand Prix.

With F1 returning to Madrid for the first time since 1981 as the capital city takes over from Barcelona as the Spanish Grand Prix host, the locals were left disappointed as both Williams' Carlos Sainz and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso were knocked out in Q1, with the former demoted from 17th to 20th by a grid penalty for impeding.

How Norris painted 'masterpiece'

There had been high expectations for McLaren coming into the weekend given Norris had recorded back-to-back pole positions and race victories either side of the summer break at similar-style circuits before Antonelli won last weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

However, that pace failed to materialise throughout practice, and Norris' personal challenge was severely heightened when he missed almost the entirety of Friday's second session because of a gearbox failure.

Mercedes looked as though they may have it all their own way before Verstappen flashed strong pace in Q2 to suggest he was capable of contending for pole.

Then, Ferrari, who had started the weekend strongly, suddenly rediscovered their pace as Hamilton took provisional pole after the first runs in Q3.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris describes his lap which claimed him Spanish GP pole as 'one of my best'

A thrilling finale was in store, and it begun with Antonelli displacing Hamilton from pole, before the Brit improved but failed to reclaim top spot.

Attention then turned to Norris and Verstappen, who were both lighting up the timesheet with fast sector times.

Norris had a massive slide in the final corner that almost took him into the barrier. It cost him around two to three tenths of a second, but he still edged out Antonelli.

Verstappen produced the fastest middle sector of the session but couldn't keep up his speed in the final part of the lap and had to settle for third.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reflects on his Spanish Grand Prix qualifying lap, which saw the Ferrari drive secure fourth.

"It was pretty much perfect," Norris reflected. "Bar the last corner, I thought I was in the wall and the boys would have to repair the car tonight.

"It could have been a little bit better - but one of the best laps I've done."

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella shared Norris' assessment that it was one of the best laps of the reigning world champion's career.

"It was a masterpiece," Stella told Sky Sports F1. "We have seen across the whole weekend, if we put it altogether, we are not far from the best cars.

"We worked our way step by step to try to put all the performance together. Lando did it only on the final run in Q3 and in the final corner he made a mistake of three tenths. It was an incredible lap - one of the best of his life until the last corner."

Sports.title: Boro strike late to beat Norwich in epic encounter
Sports.content:
Ashley Phillips was the unlikely late match-winner as Middlesbrough edged a seven-goal thriller, beating Norwich 4-3 at Riverside Stadium.

The Canaries, looking for a third win on the bounce, made the perfect start with just 50 seconds on the clock when striker Mohamed Toure hammered in, but within six more minutes Boro had gone ahead.

Sebastian Berhalter, signed from Vancouver Whitecaps this summer, powered in his first Middlesbrough goal to level things.

Exciting winger Amario Cozier-Duberry, making his first league start since arriving on loan from Brighton, then got the Riverside crowd bouncing with a tidy finish a few minutes later.

And Norwich fell further behind when Berhalter added his second in the 36th sixth minute to put Kim Hellberg's side in the driving seat.

Norwich fought back when Jovon Makama's predatory finish 20 minutes from time was followed by an equaliser from fellow substitute Jacob Wright five minutes later.

However, defender Phillips - with his first league career goal after arriving from Tottenham - popped up in the area with the killer blow to secure a third straight home win for Middlesbrough.

Norwich got things rolling early on after Andre Brooks brilliantly kept the ball in play. Alfie Jones was outmuscled by Toure before he fired powerfully in off the far post.

Less than three minutes later Berhalter levelled. The American hammered a finish in off the underside of the crossbar after a horrible turn from Ruairi McConville allowed Tommy Conway and Will Lankshear to create the opening.

Middlesbrough claimed the lead less than three minutes later in style.

A precise cross-field ball from Berhalter was chested down exquisitely by Conway. He ran at his marker before squaring to Cozier-Duberry, who curled a low finish inside Vladan Kovacevic's bottom right corner.

There were chances at both ends after that but Middlesbrough, after goalkeeper Radek Vitek had made a fine one-handed stop to deny Brooks, extended their advantage before the break.

It was Berhalter again who was in the right place to turn Callum Brittain's scuffed shot beyond a wrong-footed Kovacevic.

After the restart chances were more limited until Norwich introduced their substitutes.

Wright and Makama combined for the latter to beat Vitek and pull a goal back in the 70th minute, and they had the hope they needed.

Soon after Wright had levelled himself. He was left in acres of space to find Anthony Musaba. After the winger's shot was saved, Wright was in place to turn the loose ball high into the net.

However, Middlesbrough were not finished either. Phillips completed the scoring in the dying seconds, capitalising on Lankshear's pass across the area to secure a dramatic three points.

The managers

Middlesbrough's Kim Hellberg:

"If you look at the game as a neutral, it was a fantastic game. This was two teams that does everything they can to win the game.

"In that way it was a fantastic game, there was a lot of quality, the best version of football that I like - two teams going at each other is brilliant.

"We were the better team over 90 minutes, even though we played a very strong team. I am happy with that and it was down to the character of the boys and getting the win when things weren't going our way second half.

"The strong thing for this group is how they support each other. I see so many who were outside the squad who today celebrated like it was important for them; that is not always how it is but this group is fantastic like that.

"I need to help the players know what we should do better to win the games. Game management is a massive thing. The character of the players won us the game."

Norwich's Philippe Clement:

"It was a frantic game, with two teams really going to win.

"The biggest disappointment was not the first goal against but the 30 minutes after. I saw two/three players starting to doubt, they were not brave enough on the ball. We didn't show the football we can play.

"I wanted to see another phase of the team (after half-time) and we then showed our qualities - the team did brilliantly. The biggest memory of this game was how good we can be if everyone goes full.

"It felt like a boxing fight. I felt Middlesbrough were on the ropes in the last 10 minutes, but in the dying seconds we got the punch where we go down and we lose.

"But I'm proud of what my team showed in the second half. We will have a good season if we do that in the next days and months.

"Everyone who watched the game will have enjoyed the game - seven goals. But I'm gutted now that we don't get points from this game because we deserved this."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Swansea see off struggling Burnley
Sports.content:
Swansea moved back into the automatic promotion places as they piled more misery on new Burnley boss Nicky Hayen, whose side slumped to the bottom of the Championship with a 3-1 defeat.

The victory took Vitor Matos' side level on points with West Ham at the top of the table and erased the memory of the 3-1 midweek mauling at Southampton. For Burnley, it was a fourth defeat in seven league games and they are still awaiting their first win.

Both goals they conceded in the first half were avoidable and had their shooting been more precise they could have been at least on level terms.

Hayen was able to include former Leicester and England striker Jamie Vardy in his matchday squad for the first time following the 39-year-old's transfer from Serie A side Cremonese.

He finally made his debut as a 64th-minute substitute and had the ball in the Swansea net nine minutes later only to have the goal ruled out for offside.

Burnley started well enough and the first chance of the game fell to striker Zeki Amdouni in the eighth minute.

Having held off Stephen Welsh in the race for a ball into the Swansea box he then shot into the side-netting from a good angle.

The home side opened the scoring in the 14th minute when Adam Idah grabbed his third goal of the season. Chasing a long ball through the centre he first held off Igor Julio and then ran on to challenge Burnley goalkeeper Max Weiss just outside his box.

Weiss waited too long, lost the ball when challenged by Idah and then had to watch the striker calmly stroke the ball into an empty net.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Goalkeeper Max Weiss' catastrophic mistake saw Swansea take an early lead against Burnley.

Worse followed in the 33rd minute after Burnley had had a significant period of pressure.

But when their third corner in a row was cleared, Ugo Raghouber gave the ball away and Elijah Just picked it up in the centre circle before sending Moussa Yeo on a solo run at goal from halfway.

He got to the edge of the area before putting the ball into the bottom-left corner to notch his first goal in a Swansea shirt.

Despite going two goals down, Burnley created a number of chances and Aaron Ramsey forced Lawrence Vigouroux into a brilliant one-handed save as he tipped his rasping shot onto the crossbar.

The visitors finally scored in the 58th minute when Largie Ramazani beat the offside trap and fired past Vigouroux with a low shot into the left corner. That gave the Clarets renewed hope of getting something out of the game, but Swansea added a third goal five minutes later.

Marco Stamenic threaded the ball through for Ronald to chase and after outpacing Lucas Pires he pulled the ball across the box to give Zan Vipotnik the easiest of tap ins.

Burnley had the ball in the Swansea net once again in the 87th minute from an inswinging corner but referee James Bell spotted interference on Vigouroux and ruled it out.

The managers

Swansea's Vitor Matos:

"It was a good game for us and it was quite complete in different phases. We had really good moments when we had the ball, important moments that gave us the initiative and control in the right positions.

"That allowed us to push Burnley back and deep.

"Nothing has changed for us. The most important thing is that we keep focusing on the process, on what we can improve, when we need to improve and then on the games.

"Then the results will speak for themselves. We need to keep improving our game and individually."

Burnley's Nicky Hayen:

"It's a must-win game for us against Derby. There are no excuses, but there are clear reasons for our current situation.

"We're missing a lot of players and several new signings do not yet have the match fitness we need.

"I mentioned a few weeks ago that we had to survive until the international break, where we can finally work properly on the training pitch.

"But surviving means taking points and winning games, which we haven't managed to do enough. That makes this a difficult period, but Saturday is a must-win.

"Despite the results, we are growing as a team. What we desperately need is one victory to reward the performance and rebuild confidence.

"One win will change a lot for us - everyone is craving that feeling again. You can hold me accountable for not winning games, but there are also realistic factors such as injuries, lack of fitness and integrating new signings late.

"I'll keep working exactly as I always do. I treat every game as if it were my last, because that keeps you sharp and injects energy into the squad and tomorrow I will put that energy back into the group."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Glasner haunts Emery again as Forest win at Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest beat Aston Villa 2-1 at Villa Park to leave Unai Emery's side still searching for their first Premier League victory of the season.

Once again, Oliver Glasner got the better of Emery, who remains winless in eight matches against the Austrian.

Liam Delap went some way to paying back his £50m fee as he fired Forest in front after just 45 seconds of the second half.

Villa needed inspiration and Emery turned to his new signings Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye. The changes injected much-needed energy into the hosts and they were rewarded when Alysson struck his first goal for the club to level.

Image: Aston Villa's Alysson celebrates scoring his sides equaliser

At that point, momentum appeared to be swinging Villa's way.

However, with 10 minutes remaining, Ian Maatsen was forced off after hobbling badly. Villa had already used all their substitutes, leaving them with 10 men for the closing stages.

Forest sensed an opportunity and they took it.

With just two minutes remaining, Igor Jesus found the decisive finish to send the travelling Forest supporters wild.

Emery is having to rebuild following a turbulent summer, where a host of key players were sold, but progress is slow. The result leaves Villa with just one point from their first four games and in the bottom three.

Emery fumes over McAtee tackle on Maatsen: 'It's a red card'

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports said:

"We played the first half like we planned, we dominate, we didn't concede so much. We didn't score, but we were playing in the way we wanted. The second half, completely different. I don't know why, but we started so poor. They scored and they were creating chances.

Image: Ian Maatsen hobbled off after a tackle from James McAtee leaving Villa down to 10-men

"We corrected it and in that moment maybe we should keep the same way we were, but we couldn't. And the injury of Ian Maatsen was a key moment because the tackle was strong. And we were finishing the last 15 minutes with one player less for one tackle and they were playing with 11. For me, VAR should be there. I think it's a red card.

"If I was in the VAR and I was a referee, it was a red card."

Glasner remaining humble despite unbeaten Emery record

Oliver Glasner speaking about his record over Emery:

"I spoke to him before the game, and it's still 5-2 for him, five European trophies to two. So I said to myself, 'Oliver Glasner, stay humble'.

"And this is how I will stay. Every win is great, but I didn't play one second today. The players deserve all the credit because they did so well. And our fans deserve the credit because they supported us."

Sports.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
Sports.content:
The chants from the away end about winning the league were sung in jest, but Hull continue to show they are here to stay. Sergej Jakirovic’s dogged, intelligent side are third in the Premier League after extending their unbeaten start to four games and can even count themselves unfortunate not to have beaten another of the Big Six after pushing Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing battle at a frustrated Stamford Bridge.

Hull were 2-1 up at half-time and they had the chances to snatch the points during the second half. It took two big saves from Emiliano Martínez to prevent an upset, but this was not a good day for the Chelsea goalkeeper or his new teammates. He was one of several at fault when Hull, having dusted themselves down after conceding from Morgan Rogers early on, went ahead through Mohamed Belloumi’s quickfire double. The ease with which Chelsea’s advantage was handed over left the normally calm and considered Xabi Alonso accusing his side of being “soft” without the ball.

Alonso craves the comfort of a forgettable win. Chelsea have been exhilarating in attack, but they cannot defend. They are conceding two goals per game and the basketball nature of Alonso’s approach has created chaos rather than control. “It’s all entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win,” he said. “It will take time. When we get the lead you still need to be competing and not to give the chance so easily for them to come back.

“Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances, but that changed the mood. We will get better, but it’s having an impact on our performances.”

It is ridiculous that Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro are having to do so much in attack. Chelsea led after seven minutes, surging forward when they left four players forward at a Hull corner. João Pedro’s pass reached Rogers and the £117m signing from Aston Villa drove past Regan Slater before beating Konstantinos Tzolaki at his near post with a low, hard and early shot from the left.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro fires home Chelsea’s equaliser in the second half. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

Chelsea should have pushed on after becoming the first side to breach Hull since their promotion. Pedro Neto tested Tzolakis from the right, but the hosts became vague and complacent. This was the first time they have dominated possession in a league game this season and the result was not convincing. Hull limited them to an xG of 0.89, highlighting Chelsea’s issues against low blocks, and were clinical when they attacked.

The soft defending Alonso referenced for the equaliser started with Malo Gusto failing to deal with a long punt from Tzolakis in the 28th minute. Ryan Giles outmuscled the right-back and hooked a cross to the far post. Jorrel Hato misread the Hull left-back’s delivery, leaving Belloumi to rap a shot past Martínez.

Chelsea are without a win against promoted sides in five home games. They do not smell danger, while Alonso’s decision to leave Maxence Lacroix out at centre-back and shift from a back three to a 4-2-3-1 system backfired. Hull had so much space on the flanks. They pushed again and Belloumi’s flick found Lewie Coyle, who ran off Rogers but saw his shot cleared off the line by Levi Colwill.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it,” Alonso said. “Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

There was no response from Chelsea after Colwill turned Coyle’s shot wide. A corner came in from the left, Martínez flapped and Semi Ajayi’s header hit the bar. The ball came to Belloumi, whose shot flew in thanks to a deflection.

Alonso reacted at half-time, Hato making way for Pep Chavarría at left-back. Reece James drew a save from Tzolakis with a free-kick but Hull carried a threat on the break. They almost extended their lead when Martínez spilled a shot from Slater.

Martínez redeemed himself, blocking the rebound from McBurnie, and Chelsea soon levelled. Palmer, otherwise quiet, surprised Hull with a direct run. The No 10 drove down the left and picked out João Pedro, who lashed a shot into the roof of the net.

Hull refused to lie down. Ajayi, Giles and John Egan were outstanding at the back and the visitors maintained their shape when losing Nobel Mendy after a nasty collision with João Pedro.

Jakirovic made bold substitutions. Alonso threw Danny Welbeck on. Palmer scooped over from 20 yards and Tzolakis thwarted Rogers, but Hull had the best chance. Giles crossed again and Mohamed-Ali Cho shot straight at Martínez from close range.

Hull settled for a point. Jakirovic quashed talk of qualifying for Europe, insisting that survival remains the aim. The Bosnian has everyone pulling in the same direction. Before the start of the season he told his staff he would give them seven days off if Hull took eight points from their first five games. Mission completed with a game to spare.

Sports.title: Frustrated Liverpool lack any spark as Fulham claim deserved first point
Sports.content:
Álvaro Arbeloa was often the obstacle to Andoni Iraola’s international ambitions back in the days when both were vying for a right-back role with Spain. On his return to Anfield, and under the watchful eye of former manager Rafael Benítez, Arbeloa thwarted Iraola once again to claim his first Premier League point as Fulham head coach against an ineffective Liverpool.

Fulham belied their lowly position and run of three league defeats to take a merited point from a Liverpool team that was a pale imitation of the one that beat Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday. Iraola fielded a front four that cost almost £400m but the most impressive forward on display was the Fulham academy graduate Josh King. The draw was Liverpool’s third in four league games under their new head coach and the seventh in 12 Premier League matches at Anfield in 2026. Progress can be painfully slow at times.

“It is the first game we’ve had problems creating chances and making the difference offensively,” Iraola said. “It is easy for me to say the players were tired (after Atlético). There was a lack of freshness and, we cannot hide it, it was the worst turnaround in terms of 60-70 hours. But this is going to happen in the season and we have to adapt. Sometimes you need a set play or a moment of brilliance to win these kind of games but we were not as good offensively as other games.”

Liverpool were sluggish and sloppy – Florian Wirtz and Kostas Tsimikas put simple passes straight out of play in the first half, setting the tone for a disjointed performance – while Fulham bypassed the central midfield pairing of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch repeatedly. The visitors’ confidence and composure on the ball, along with their defensive organisation, was hugely impressive considering the start to the season under the former Real Madrid interim coach and Liverpool defender. With more conviction in front of goal, Arbeloa’s side could have capitalised on Liverpool’s malaise.

Bradley Barcola created an early, difficult chance for Alexander Isak that the striker swept wide of the far post. Victor Muñoz went closer still with a glancing header from a Szoboszlai corner. Bernd Leno, the Fulham goalkeeper, reacted superbly to claw the ball away. But that was the sum total of Liverpool’s first-half enterprise.

Fulham were gifted a glorious opportunity when Alisson played a ridiculous pass to Gravenberch, who was under pressure from Sander Berge. Berge’s challenge fell to King, who was sent flying by the Liverpool goalkeeper but the referee, Thomas Bramall, played a good advantage as Gonzalo García received the loose ball. García had time to pick his spot but Jérémy Jacquet blocked his shot in front of the goalline.

View image in fullscreen Jérémy Jacquet clears the ball off the line to deny Fulham the lead. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

The visitors prospered down their left and Oscar Bobb missed another good opening when, unmarked and 18 yards out, he miscontrolled Alex Iwobi’s pinpoint delivery. Jacquet came to Liverpool’s rescue once again seconds later when preventing García breaking through with an excellent challenge.

Liverpool were deserving of a few home truths during the break – chiefly, you would have been lambasted for this last season under Arne Slot – and performed with more intensity in the second half. But not with any more threat. The introductions of Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Milos Kerkez brought modest improvement but Fulham continued to contain the hosts comfortably. The new signing David Affengruber had a fine debut and Calvin Bassey was commanding against Isak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors remained dangerous on the counterattack and Alisson pushed away a King effort that was heading for the top corner. King’s replacement, Rodrigo Muniz, let a decent chance run away from him inside the area and the substitute Kevin dragged a shot wide from 18 yards. Isak finally escaped Bassey’s attentions in stoppage time but his flicked header from a Szoboszlai corner sailed wide.

Arbeloa said: “When you are not winning games it’s not so easy for your players to believe in your ideas. But they believe in the way we have been working and I showed them the things that we were doing so well. We were more balanced and controlled the transitions well. I’m happy with the point but more with the performance of my players and the character, the personality and the ambition they showed in this stadium.”

Sports.title: London City’s superstars brought down to earth in WSL defeat at West Ham
Sports.content:
West Ham claimed their first Women’s Super League win of the season with a 2-1 home victory over London City Lionesses. Kelly Gago put the Hammers ahead after 21 minutes, racing between the centre-backs Mapi León and Isa Kardinaal to latch on to Seraina Piubel’s pass from nearly halfway and rounding Elene Lete in the London City goal.

Daniëlle van de Donk was denied an equaliser when Constance Picaud-Inconnu saved low, with Alexia Putellas, another of London City’s big-name summer signings, lifting the rebound over the bar under the challenge of Inès Belloumou.

View image in fullscreen Kelly Gago is congratulated after scoring the opener. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

Viviane Asseyi doubled West Ham’s lead three minutes after the break after being released by Riko Ueki, running the length of the London City half before firing home.

London City set up a frantic finish after Van de Donk’s clever backheel from Kadidiatou Diani’s low cross crept in at the near post 14 minutes from time.

View image in fullscreen Danielle van de Donk flicks home for the Lionesses. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

The veteran Netherlands forward had scored a similar goal with the winner against Manchester United on the opening weekend – this defeat at Chigwell Construction Stadium was a reality check for Maestre’s side as they seek to challenge the top teams in the WSL.

West Ham bounced back after their defeat to Tottenham. “I saw the spirit that I want to see every time, it’s part of our identity,” said their head coach, Rita Guarino. “We can’t forget that we have this kind of value and we need to show it in every single game.”

Sports.title: Emery takes responsibility as Forest strike late at winless Aston Villa
Sports.content:
This summer there were a couple of significant pieces of the puzzle for Oliver Glasner to put into place at Nottingham Forest. The first was a mobile striker to lead the line and the other was a right wing-back to fit his favoured 3-4-3 system. Enter Liam Delap and Daniel Muñoz, both of whom had a big say in Forest’s first win under Glasner, though the match-winner was one of the old brigade in Igor Jesus.

Delap registered his first Forest goal in style, a powerful shot from 25 yards and Muñoz was involved in the slick move that culminated in Igor Jesus reading Morgan Gibbs-White’s exquisite backheel to down Aston Villa, who remain winless in the Premier League.

That the winner came down Villa’s left made things even more painful from their perspective. For the final 12 minutes, including six in stoppage time, John McGinn was operating as an emergency left-back after Ian Maatsen’s injury reduced them to 10 men. By the 63rd minute, after sending on Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye for their Villa debuts, Unai Emery had used all five substitutions; Pau Torres was forced off with a hamstring problem midway through the first half that could sideline him for a month and Tammy Abraham and Alysson, who pulled Villa level, arrived at the interval. Abraham replaced Jackson, who Emery felt was at risk of a second yellow card.

Those changes left Villa unable to replace Maatsen after the full-back was cynically fouled by James McAtee, whom Emery felt should have been sent off for the challenge. Emery said the video assistant referee, Timothy Wood, should have flagged the incident to the referee, Andy Madley. “It’s a clear tackle behind the player and, for me, it should be a red card,” he said. “But it’s not an excuse for how we played the second half. We played so poorly and this is my responsibility.”

View image in fullscreen Unai Emery, the Aston Villa head coach, is without a win in the Premier League this season. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

For the second successive season, Villa are winless in their opening four league matches and for so long it seemed they would again fail to score. Alysson’s header from McGinn’s dainty cross after a short corner meant they were spared ruminating on the moment Matz Sels twice denied Victor Lindelöf. In between Sels repelling Lindelöf with his feet and taking his side-foot shot to the face, Murillo smacked an attempted clearance against his own post. Lindelöf has scored one goal in almost six years, his last in November 2023.

Villa were rattled by Forest seizing the lead 45 seconds into the second half. Murillo dispossessed Emiliano Buendía, snapping into a challenge after Boubacar Kamara’s flick and then Delap jinked clear of Ross Barkley. Delap’s next couple of touches took the ball out of his feet, dribbling diagonally across the pitch before sending an unerring right-foot shot into the Villa net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Emery sent on Mbaye and Manzambi in place of Buendía and Barkley but their arrivals did not bring instant success. Instead Delap thought he had doubled his and Forest’s tally, only for the offside flag and a VAR check to deny him. A few moments earlier Tyrone Mings, a first-half substitute for the injured Torres, made a desperate block to thwart Dan Ndoye after superb holdup play by Delap.

Forest, without key defenders Nikola Milenkovic and Jair Cunha through injury, had been readying Igor Jesus when Villa scored, but the striker still arrived to replace Ndoye, who, after a first-half collision with Maatsen, was left with what Glasner described as “a nose like a boxer in the 12th round”. At that point, Villa Park was primed for a grandstand finale, but Forest also roused. Zion Suzuki was twice called into action, his best save clambering down to his right to keep out a Xaver Schlager header, but then Igor Jesus popped up with the winner.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap (right) opened his account for Nottingham Forest with a 46th-minute strike. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Muñoz exchanged passes with Gibbs-White, who eliminated three Villa defenders with a sumptuous flick before Igor Jesus coolly passed the ball past Suzuki to maintain Glasner’s pristine record against Emery. Glasner has not lost in eight meetings against Emery, winning six and drawing two.

“I spoke to him before the game and it’s still 5-2 for him, five European trophies to two,” said Forest’s head coach. “So I said to myself: ‘Oliver Glasner, stay humble.’ And this is how I will stay. The players deserve all the credit, because they did so well, and our fans deserve credit because they supported us, and so now we all go back and will have a lovely Saturday evening.”

Sports.title: Flemming and Ipswich floor 10-man Crystal Palace with 90th-minute winner
Sports.content:
This victory has been a long time coming for Gary O’Neil. The Millwall supporter from Beckenham, whose son plays for Crystal Palace’s academy, had picked up a solitary point on his previous five trips to this part of south London as a manager. So it was no wonder that he celebrated Zian Flemming’s winning goal in the 90th minute with the same gusto as the travelling Ipswich supporters.

On a topsy-turvy afternoon Palace took the lead before Emersonn and Leif Davis cancelled out Anan Khalaili’s first goal for Palace after Axel Disasi’s red card. Jørgen Strand Larsen equalised with 15 minutes remaining but Khalaili had his head in his hands after missing an open goal minutes later and it was to prove crucial as Flemming – the last of the 14 new players signed by Ipswich in the summer in a record spend of £190m for a promoted side – scrambled home the winner after Davis hit the crossbar with a looping header.

Ipswich managed 22 points when they were in the Premier League two years ago, but look far better equipped to survive this time around. “I don’t care where I win, as long as I win,” said O’Neill of ending his Selhurst Park run without a victory. “It’s been the best four months of my career, playing or managing. I’ve loved it, every minute of it. The playing group just gives everything. We’ll lose some, but we’ll give everything when we lose.”

The chances of either side keeping a clean sheet looked slim given Palace have not managed one in the Premier League since April and Ipswich have conceded 58 goals since their last in December 2024 – a run of 23 matches. Palace badly missed their captain, Dean Henderson, who was absent due to injury, and Pierre Sage may regret showing his ruthless streak by dropping Jaydee Canvot for what he described as “a sporting decision” after being unhappy with his performances in training.

While 18-year-old Honest Ahanor did well on his debut, Walter Benítez was at fault for Flemming’s winner that means Palace have lost their opening two home games of a Premier League season for the first time since 2018 and conceded more goals than any other team in the division.

“I need more from him and I’m sure he is able to give that,” said Sage of Canvot’s omission from the matchday squad. “I don’t care about my authority. I want the players at 100% of what they are able to do. And when they give less, I have to shake them.”

View image in fullscreen Leif Davis nods home Ipswich’s second. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Like Palace, Ipswich had conceded eight goals from their opening three matches and it was easy to see why. Kjell Scherpen was extremely fortunate to get away with a misplaced pass that went straight to Adam Wharton but Palace’s stand-in captain scuffed his shot with the goal gaping.

The hosts were ahead three minutes later when Ipswich lost the ball cheaply in midfield and Daichi Kamada set up Khalaili to drill home his first Palace goal via a deflection off Davis. Strand Larsen would have left Ipswich with a mountain to climb if he had finished off another chance soon after. But O’Neil was given hope when Davis whipped over a cross for Emersonn to equalise. Palace’s defenders appeared to stop for a split second because they thought the left-back was offside in the buildup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Things went from bad to worse for Palace when Disasi charged recklessly into a challenge on Jack Clarke and caught him just below the knee with his studs raised. The referee, Chris Kavanagh, had no choice but to send him off.

Sage opted to withdraw Palace’s chief creative spark Yéremy Pino and replace him with another defender, Takehiro Tomiyasu. That only encouraged Ipswich to push forward, although their second goal owed more to luck than anything else. Dara O’Shea’s cross came off Emersonn’s shoulder and the ball somehow diverted straight to Davis to nod home just before the break.

Sage still looked less than impressed when he emerged for the second half. Palace’s 10 men roused themselves and Quinten Timber twice went close before Strand Larsen found the breakthrough. Kamada was the architect with a clever pass that allowed the Norway striker to hold off the challenge of Issa Diop and beat Scherpen. But it was Flemming who had the last laugh after coming off the bench as he reacted quicker than Benítez when a header from Davis came off the woodwork to leave O’Neil and Ipswich’s fans celebrating a landmark win.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Middlesbrough win seven-goal thriller; Burnley lose again
Sports.content:
Ashley Phillips was the unlikely late match-winner as Middlesbrough edged a seven-goal thriller, beating Norwich 4-3 at Riverside Stadium.

The Canaries, looking for a third win on the bounce, made the perfect start with just 50 seconds on the clock when striker Mohamed Touré hammered in, but within six more minutes Boro had gone ahead. Sebastian Berhalter powered in his first Middlesbrough goal to level it, before winger Amario Cozier-Duberry had the Riverside crowd bouncing with a tidy finish a few minutes later.

Norwich fell further behind when Berhalter added his second in the 36th minute, but then fought back when Jovon Makama’s predatory finish 20 minutes from time was followed by an equaliser from fellow substitute Jacob Wright five minutes later.

However, defender Phillips – with his first league career goal after arriving from Tottenham – popped up in the area with the killer blow to secure a third straight home win for Middlesbrough.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Leicester ease pressure on Martin with much-needed win at Stockport Show The beleaguered Leicester manager, Russell Martin, saw his side claim a much-needed win in a League One thriller against Stockport. The Foxes held on for a 4-3 victory at Edgeley Park, their second of the league season, after a double from Emil Riis and one from Johan Lundstram had put Leicester three goals in front. Jack Diamond had cancelled out Liam Cullen’s early opener for Leicester, and two goals in four minutes from Oliver Norwood and Kyle Wootton put the pressure right on the visitors, but they did not buckle. Sheffield Wednesday, the leaders, dropped points at home as they were held to a goalless draw by Wigan, while it was the same score for second-placed Huddersfield at Mansfield despite the Stags having Owen Dodgson sent off only moments after he came on at half-time. Bradford sit only one point off the top thanks to George Pratt, whose first EFL goal earned a 1-0 win to end Notts County’s unbeaten start to the campaign. Managerless Wycombe claimed their first victory of the season, triumphing 3-2 at Leyton Orient. Tom Hounsell, who took the interim reins after Michael Duff’s dismissal this week, saw the new signing Jayden Wareham make it two goals in two matches before Jack Grimmer’s own goal pulled Orient level. Fred Onyedinma put Wanderers back ahead just before half-time and Dan Harvie doubled the lead moments after the break, but Jaze Kabia quickly reduced the deficit again. Cambridge are up to fourth after goals from Liam Bennett and Kelland Watts enabled them to come from behind to beat Reading 2-1, while two very late strikes from Louie Sibley and Gatlin O’Donkor earned Oxford a 3-0 success against Burton. Plymouth were also 3-0 winners, Olivier Irow, Ronan Curtis and Aribim Pepple scoring against Barnsley, while bottom-placed Doncaster lost again, Myles Hippolyte scoring in a 1-0 victory for AFC Wimbledon. An entertaining encounter between Blackpool and Bromley ended 2-2, and Chris Conn-Clarke levelled late on for Peterborough in a 1-1 draw with MK Dons. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Cyle Larin scored twice as Southampton hammered Bristol City 4-1 at St Mary’s. Larin scored in either half, with late goals from Kuryu Matsuki and Finn Azaz after Lorent Tolaj had pulled one back for visitors City. The Saints are formidable opposition at St Mary’s and have not lost on their own patch since January.

Swansea moved back into the automatic promotion places as they piled more misery on the new Burnley manager Nicky Hayen, whose side slumped to the bottom of the table with a 3-1 defeat. The victory took Vitor Matos’ side level on points with West Ham at the top. For Burnley, it was a fourth defeat in seven league games and they are still awaiting their first win.

View image in fullscreen Nicky Hayen reacts as his Burnley side sink to the bottom of the Championship. Photograph: Steven Paston/PA

Both goals they conceded in the first half were avoidable and had their shooting been more precise they could have been at least on level terms. The former Leicester and England striker Jamie Vardy came on with half an hour left, and had the ball in the Swansea net nine minutes later only for the goal to be ruled out for offside.

Hayen layer described next weekend’s home match with Derby as a “must-win game”, adding: “I mentioned a few weeks ago that we had to survive until the international break, where we can finally work properly on the training pitch.

“But surviving means taking points and winning games, which we haven’t managed to do enough. What we desperately need is one victory to reward the performance and rebuild confidence. I’ll keep working exactly as I always do. I treat every game as if it were my last, because that keeps you sharp and injects energy into the squad and tomorrow I will put that energy back into the group.”

Chris Davies said his Birmingham side are heading in the right direction after they fought back to win 2-1 at Derby. Davies saw his players dig in through more than 13 minutes of added time to secure a second league win of the season. Derby had gone ahead against the run of play in the 40th minute through Bobby Clark. Birmingham’s response was instant with Carlos Vicente heading in at the back post from Liam Millar’s cross. They scored again in the 64th minute when Paik Seung-Ho headed in a corner for his first goal since December.

View image in fullscreen Birmingham keeper James Beadle celebrates with fans after their win at Pride Park. Photograph: Lee Keuneke/PA

Davies said: “We’ve looked a completely different team to last season, not only stylistically but just the strength and mental strength. It pains me to say it but we would have lost that game last season.”

Steven Schumacher hailed Bolton goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu’s “outstanding” display after a 1-0 victory over Cardiff. Substitute Thierry Gale headed in a last-minute winner to earn Wanderers only a second win since returning to the Championship as last season’s League One play-off champions. The former Southampton and Stoke keeper contributed 10 saves, including a stunning second-half stop to deny Yousef Salech’s close-range header.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Charlie Lakin scores twice as Barnet beat Accrington and go top Show Barnet took over at the top of League Two after they beat Accrington 2-1 and Bristol Rovers lost 2-0 to Grimsby. Charlie Lakin’s double enabled Barnet to come from behind after Charlie Caton’s first-half opener, with Devon Matthews seeing red for Stanley. Rovers were also reduced to 10 men, but Tommy Leigh’s dismissal came when they were already 2-0 down after goals for Kieran Green and Geza David Turi. York are a point back after a 4-0 thumping of 10-man Swindon, in-form Alex Newby scoring twice, and Cheltenham also sit on 11 points thanks to a 3-1 win over Crawley. Dylan Morgan opened the scoring early on for Crawley, but two goals for Charlie McCann and one for Andreas Weimann turned the tables. A topsy-turvy clash between Rotherham and Salford ended 3-3, with the Ammies going from two up to 3-2 down and having Abraham Odoh sent off but Macaulay Langstaff equalised from the penalty spot. Port Vale are off the bottom thanks to George Byers’ penalty in a 1-0 win over Exeter and are replaced by Rochdale, who drew 0-0 with Walsall. Shrewsbury and Gillingham were 2-0 winners against Northampton and Tranmere, respectively, while Chesterfield defeated Oldham 2-1. Colchester and Crewe played out a 1-1 draw, as did Newport and Fleetwood. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Dapo Afolayan’s double helped Blackburn secure a much-needed 3-1 win over Millwall at a discontented Ewood Park. The game had not kicked off before the first “Venky’s out’’ chants could be heard but Afolayan, who turned 29 on Friday, gave the home fans something to cheer with a deft improvised flick to open the scoring in the 41st minute.

Although Lydon Dykes’ penalty levelled matters six minutes after the restart, Afolayan’s thumping strike around the hour mark restored the lead. Rovers managed the closing stages well and substitute Andri Gudjohnsen made the game safe in stoppage time with a breakaway goal to end a four-game winless run.

Jack McGlynn orchestrated Stoke’s first away win since January with a deserved 2-1 success at Watford. A 1-1 draw at Cardiff in midweek had ended a sequence of nine consecutive defeats away from Staffordshire, and the Potters were good value for their first win in 11 road trips – and their third success in four league games. McGlynn opened the scoring for Stoke on half-time with Eric Bocat doubling the lead 13 minutes into the second half. Amin Nabizada’s reply came too late for the Hornets.

Watford’s manager, Alessio Dionisi, said: “My players are tired: it’s normal when you play every three days for 10 matches, and we are a good team when we have them all available, but I know our situation. If we stick together and we believe in the future, I’m sure the future will be better.”

Callum Styles earned West Brom a point as they came from behind to draw 1-1 against QPR at The Hawthorns. QPR led through a Chris Mepham own goal in the 38th minute which came completely against the run of play. That lead lasted just three minutes as Styles equalised to extend the Baggies’ unbeaten home record to 11 games, while Rangers have yet to lose on their travels this season.

Freddie Draper came off the bench to net a late winner in a hard-fought 1-0 win for Lincoln away at Preston. Draper headed in Andrei Coubis’ long throw in the 81st minute. The Imps are now unbeaten in their last four league games, while Preston’s nightmare start continues, with three points from the first 21 available.

Lincoln’s joint head coach Tom Shaw praised his side for perfecting “the real ugly side of football … we’re very proud of how we play. We’ve recruited, nurtured and developed a set of players that have got incredible character. We pride ourselves on those horrible, ugly things.”

Charlton maintained their unbeaten home record this season with a 0-0 draw against Portsmouth. The game may have lacked goals, but it was not devoid of entertainment, particularly in an open second half.
